key_insight: High asynchrony in off-policy policy-gradient RL for LLMs creates heavy-tailed importance ratios from stale rollouts, which dramatically increases gradient variance; controlling the tails of those ratios enables stable, high-throughput asynchronous training.
problem_solved: Reduces the extreme variance and instability that arise when widely-used critic-free policy-gradient methods (e.g., REINFORCE, GRPO) train on stale, off-policy rollouts in asynchronous LLM training pipelines.
method: Diagnose variance source: show stale rollouts produce heavy-tailed importance ratios that let a few samples dominate updates.
Introduce variance-control for off-policy gradients (staleness-aware weighting / tail-bounding of importance ratios) to suppress heavy tails and limit per-sample influence.
Integrate the variance-controlled estimator into an asynchronous training pipeline to preserve end-to-end throughput while stabilizing learning.
impact: Enables more reliable and scalable RL fine-tuning of LLMs by keeping asynchronous throughput high without sacrificing stability—reducing catastrophic gradient spikes and improving sample efficiency and convergence.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: asynchronous data producers → replay/staleness buffer → policy update, annotated to show stale rollouts feeding the learner.
Side-by-side density plots: heavy-tailed importance-ratio distribution before vs. compacted/tail-bounded distribution after variance control.
Line chart: training stability metrics (variance or reward curves) vs. throughput, showing improved stability at high asynchrony with the proposed method.
Icon set: LLM + policy gradient symbol, warning/explosion icon for variance spikes, and shield icon for variance control/stability.
paper_title: Stable Asynchrony: Variance-Controlled Off-Policy RL for LLMs
paper_authors: Luke Huang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Qinghao Hu, Shang Yang, Song Han
